title: A parameter in a reduced local curve localizes to the total fraction ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring (with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$), reduced (having no nonzero nilpotent elements), and of Krull dimension exactly one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A nonzerodivisor is an element $t$ such that $tr=0$ implies $r=0$ for every $r\in R$. Let $T$ be its set of nonzerodivisors, and $Q=T^{-1}R$ its total ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For an ideal $I$, write $\sqrt I=\{x\in R: x^n\in I\text{ for some integer }n\geq1\}$. There exists $f\in\mathfrak m$ which is a nonzerodivisor and belongs to no minimal prime ideal (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime), such that $\sqrt{fR}=\mathfrak m$ and the canonical $R$-algebra map $R_f\to Q$ is an isomorphism, where $R_f$ is localization at the powers of $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].
